summary: An indeterminate wait, announced once. A ring plus a politely-announced label, sized off the icon ramp.
useWhen: work is in flight and its duration cannot be measured
a control has started something and must show it is working
a small region is waiting and a skeleton would be more scaffolding than content

useInstead.when: the work has a measurable fraction complete
useInstead.why: a spinner over measurable work discards information the user wants — a spinner and a 90%-complete upload look identical

useInstead.when: a region is being replaced by content with a known shape
useInstead.why: a skeleton holds the layout so it does not jump when content lands; a spinner leaves a hole that then reflows

sm.use: inside a control, or beside a line of text

md.use: the default — a panel or a section

lg.use: a whole route or a full-page wait

requires: a `label` naming what is loading — it is announced politely and is the only thing a screen-reader user receives
`isDecorative` when something else already announces the wait, so two live regions do not race
notes: the ring is aria-hidden; the label carries the meaning
prefers-reduced-motion slows the rotation rather than stopping it — a stationary spinner is indistinguishable from a hung one

antiPatterns.why: role="status" creates a live region; an EMPTY live region announces nothing. This exact half-measure appeared in 48 files of this repo's eval corpus
the button label already says it. Two live regions announcing the same wait talk over each other

antiPatterns.dont: a Spinner for an upload that reports bytes transferred
antiPatterns.why: throwing away a known percentage makes a finite wait feel unbounded
